summary: SPHEREx Sky Blink is an interactive web application designed to democratize access to NASA's SPHEREx near-infrared survey data. We developed a high-performance Python backend (FastAPI, Astropy) that dynamically fetches, aligns, and processes raw FITS images from IRSA, paired with a sleek frontend that renders these images as animated time-lapse films. To address the challenge, our tool emulates the highly successful citizen science tool "WiseView", translating dense astronomical data into accessible visual streams. Users can explore any patch of the sky, apply static sky subtraction to highlight moving objects, stack exposures for depth, and overlay multi-mission data from Gaia DR3 and AllWISE. This project is important because it bridges the gap between complex raw space data and the general public. By making the dynamic infrared universe visually intuitive, SPHEREx Sky Blink empowers citizen scientists to discover hidden phenomena such as brown dwarfs, variable stars, and near-Earth asteroids and transforming passive data archives into an accessible engine for widespread astronomical discovery.
details:
SPHEREx Sky Blink is a public web tool that plays the SPHEREx mission's infrared sky observations as a short time-lapse film, allowing users to easily spot moving objects

The application surfaces moving targets like comets, asteroids, and brown dwarfs rapidly, serving as a fast triage tool before heavier data pipelines run. It features built-in quality cues—such as per-frame noise, flagged-pixel share, and detector wavelength—so users can confidently evaluate a detection's trustworthiness. Furthermore, the tool generates a unique URL for every setting configuration, allowing users to perfectly reproduce and share exactly what they saw.

Our goal is to open the SPHEREx mission to everyone, spanning mission scientists, students, and amateur citizen scientists. By providing a zero-install, browser-based platform, we democratize access to a massive survey of over a billion objects, turning open data into an engine for widespread public discovery.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software used

Languages & Frontend: HTML, Vanilla JavaScript, and SVG

Backend & Math: Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, and Pillow

Astronomy Libraries: Astropy, astroquery, and pyvo

Data Sources & APIs: NASA IRSA (SPHEREx archive, TAP/AllWISE), ESA Gaia DR3 archive (via VizieR), and CDS (Aladin, hips2fits)

We creatively modernized the historic "blink comparator" method—the exact technique used to discover Pluto in 1930—for a highly complex, 102-band infrared dataset. We also engineered an on-the-fly spectral extraction tool that dynamically calculates flux (minus a local ring median), alongside an automatic median-subtraction filter that elegantly cancels out the static sky, making moving objects boldly stand out as bright and dark pixel pairs.

First, we considered the immense scale of the dataset; with a billion objects in 102 bands, the data is simply "too big for human eyes" to sift through manually without specialized software. Second, we prioritized pipeline speed and resilience by implementing parallel cutout downloads, cached aligned arrays, and automatic query retries for dropped connections. Finally, we considered accessibility, ensuring the tool is entirely public by design, requires no API keys, and features an "embed mode" for seamless integration into educational notebooks and external sites.
